core_obligations: Forward direction: if A is a discrete valuation ring then A is normal, so the integral closure A' used in the definition of the delta-invariant equals A and the invariant vanishes (proof lines 8335-8336).
Converse: if the delta-invariant is zero then A is integrally closed in its total ring of fractions, which for a reduced ring forces normality (proof lines 8336-8340).
Conclude that A is a discrete valuation ring from normality, one-dimensionality and Noetherianity (proof lines 8341-8342).
proof_roadmap: Identify the vanishing condition with the integral closure being trivial.
Deduce normality from integral closedness in the total ring of fractions.
Apply the characterization of discrete valuation rings.
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises the vanishing of the delta-invariant of a reduced one-dimensional Nagata local ring A as equivalent to A being a discrete valuation ring. The proof is short but has two genuine directions: if A is a discrete valuation ring then it is normal and the integral closure A' equals A, so the quotient defining the delta-invariant is zero; conversely, vanishing means A is integrally closed in its total ring of fractions, which by the reducedness criterion makes A normal, and a one-dimensional Noetherian normal local ring is a discrete valuation ring (proof lines 8335-8342). H2: the two implications each use a different structural fact, and the second is the one that links the invariant to normality.
